Title: From Figma to Code: A Practical Handoff Checklist
Desc: Learn how designers and developers can work together effectively using a practical Figma-to-code handoff checklist that reduces confusion, speeds up development, and improves product quality.
Author: Core Lord
Data:
One of the most common sources of frustration in software projects happens between design and development.

The design looks perfect in Figma.

The finished product looks different.

Developers struggle to interpret details.

Designers wonder why the implementation doesn't match the mockup.

A proper handoff process solves many of these problems.

This guide provides a practical checklist that helps teams move from Figma designs to production-ready code with fewer misunderstandings.

---

## What Is Design Handoff?

Design handoff is the process of transferring design specifications from designers to developers.

The goal is simple:

```text
Design
↓
Implementation
↓
Accurate Final Product
```

Without a clear handoff process, teams often encounter:

Missing specifications

Incorrect spacing

Inconsistent colors

Responsive issues

Delayed releases


A structured checklist reduces these risks.


---

Why Good Handoff Matters

Poor handoffs can create:

Development delays

Extra revisions

Frustrated teams

Inconsistent user experiences


Good handoffs help:

Save time

Improve communication

Reduce assumptions

Increase design accuracy


The better the handoff, the smoother development becomes.


---



Pre-Handoff Design Checklist

Before development begins, designers should verify several items.


---

Confirm Design Completion

Avoid handing off unfinished designs.

Ensure:

Screens are finalized

User flows are approved

Stakeholder feedback is incorporated

Major changes are complete


Frequent redesigns during implementation can slow projects significantly.


---

Organize Figma Files

Messy files create confusion.

A well-organized file should include:

Clear page names

Structured layers

Logical component grouping

Consistent naming conventions


Example:

Buttons
Cards
Navigation
Forms
Modals

instead of random layer names.


---

Use Components Consistently

Reusable components improve both design and development.

Examples:

Buttons

Inputs

Cards

Navigation menus


Benefits:

Consistency

Faster implementation

Easier maintenance


Developers can map components directly to code.


---

Define Design Tokens

Document core design values.

Examples:

Colors

Primary
Secondary
Success
Warning
Error

Typography

Font Families
Font Sizes
Line Heights
Weights

Spacing

4px
8px
16px
24px
32px

Design tokens help maintain consistency.


---



Developer Handoff Checklist

Developers should review key details before writing code.


---

Check Responsive Designs

Ask:

What happens on mobile?

What happens on tablets?

What happens on large screens?


Avoid assumptions.

Responsive behavior should be documented.


---

Review Interaction States

Every interactive element should include:

Default State

Normal appearance.

Hover State

Desktop interactions.

Active State

Pressed interactions.

Focus State

Accessibility support.

Disabled State

Unavailable actions.

Missing states often lead to inconsistent implementations.


---

Verify Accessibility Requirements

Accessibility should be discussed before coding begins.

Review:

Color contrast

Keyboard navigation

Focus indicators

ARIA requirements

Semantic structure


Accessibility is easier to build early than retrofit later.


---

Identify Missing Assets

Developers should confirm availability of:

Icons

Logos

Images

Illustrations


Missing assets often create delays near launch.


---

Confirm Export Settings

Examples:

SVG
PNG
WebP

Different assets may require different formats.

Optimized assets improve performance.


---



Figma Inspection Checklist

Modern Figma tools provide valuable implementation details.

Developers should inspect:


---

Spacing

Verify:

Margins

Padding

Gaps


Avoid estimating distances visually.


---

Typography

Check:

Font size

Font weight

Line height

Letter spacing


Accurate typography significantly affects design quality.


---

Layout Structure

Understand:

Containers

Auto Layout settings

Alignment behavior

Responsive constraints


This helps replicate designs correctly.


---

Component Variants

Review component variations such as:

Primary Button
Secondary Button
Outlined Button
Disabled Button

These often map directly to code components.


---

Communication Checklist

Many handoff issues are communication issues.


---

Clarify Ambiguous Areas

If something is unclear:

Ask.

Never assume.

A five-minute conversation can save hours of rework.


---

Discuss Edge Cases

Examples:

Empty states

Loading states

Error states

Long content

Missing images


These situations are often forgotten during design.


---

Confirm Priorities

Not every screen requires immediate implementation.

Agree on:

MVP scope

Future features

Launch requirements


Clear priorities improve planning.


---



Common Handoff Mistakes

Designing Only Happy Paths

Users encounter:

Errors

Empty data

Failed requests


Design for these scenarios.


---

Missing Mobile Designs

Developers should not guess mobile behavior.

Provide responsive layouts.


---

Ignoring Accessibility

Accessibility requirements should be documented early.


---

Unorganized Figma Files

Poor structure slows everyone down.


---

Lack of Communication

Documentation helps, but conversations remain important.


---

A Practical Figma-to-Code Workflow

A typical workflow:

Design Complete
↓
Design Review
↓
Component Audit
↓
Accessibility Review
↓
Developer Handoff
↓
Implementation
↓
QA Testing
↓
Launch

Each step reduces surprises later.

[ ] Interaction states included

[ ] Accessibility reviewed

[ ] Assets exported

[ ] Edge cases considered

This checklist catches many common issues.


---

Benefits of a Good Handoff

Teams that establish strong handoff processes often experience:

Faster development

Fewer revisions

Better accessibility

More accurate implementations

Improved collaboration


Small process improvements can create significant long-term benefits.


---

FAQ

What is a Figma handoff?

A Figma handoff is the process of transferring design specifications and assets from designers to developers for implementation.

Why do design handoffs fail?

Common reasons include missing specifications, unclear communication, incomplete designs, and undocumented edge cases.

Should developers inspect Figma files directly?

Yes. Inspecting spacing, typography, layouts, and components improves implementation accuracy.

What should designers include before handoff?

Responsive layouts, interaction states, design tokens, organized components, and required assets.

Why is accessibility important during handoff?

Including accessibility requirements early helps teams build more inclusive products and reduces costly revisions later.


---

Final Thoughts

A successful Figma-to-code handoff is not just about sharing a design file. It's about creating a shared understanding between designers and developers.

When teams document design decisions, organize components, define responsive behavior, consider accessibility, and communicate clearly, implementation becomes faster and more predictable.

The best handoffs don't eliminate questions entirely—they make sure the right questions are answered before development begins.
